next.headline: MageCart: card skimmers that hit online shops and abused cloud hosting
next.in_short: MageCart is a name for groups that steal payment card numbers from online shops. Reports describe injected skimmer code, fake payment forms and abuse of cloud services such as Heroku.

sentences.t: MageCart is the name given to a group of hackers that steals credit card numbers, often by skimming card data from ecommerce sites.
WIRED says Magecart has been behind some of the bigger hacks of recent years, from British Airways to Ticketmaster.
Malwarebytes describes the crooked part of the Magecart cabal, which suggests the name covers more than one party.
According to WIRED, Magecart hackers cast the widest possible net to find vulnerable ecommerce sites.
Malwarebytes reports that the compromised sites were online shopping sites, where the skimmer code was injected.
The singular goal, WIRED says, is stealing credit card numbers.
Malwarebytes says a compromised shop gets a single line of code that loads a remote piece of JavaScript.
A rogue iframe then overlays the normal payment form to harvest the victim's card data, according to Malwarebytes.
The stolen data is sent back in encoded form, Malwarebytes reports.
Malwarebytes says the actors registered free Heroku accounts to host their skimmer infrastructure. Heroku is a cloud platform owned by Salesforce.
Malwarebytes also documented earlier skimmers served from GitHub and injected into Amazon S3 buckets, and says it will likely keep seeing skimmers abuse more cloud services.
In a WIRED article published on 2019-07-11, the reporter says the group hit 17,000 domains in a few months, which it put down to poor security hygiene.
WIRED warns that the method could lead to even bigger problems. That is a forward-looking warning, not a confirmed outcome.
Malwarebytes published its report on Heroku-hosted skimmers on 2019-12-03 and says the abusive instances were reported to Heroku and taken down.
